\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

GRPO-trained formalizers converge to high prove rates on first-order logic problems ($95{\pm}5\%$ across three seeds, 1000 steps), yet at convergence, \emph{none} produce structurally sound outputs.
Each seed develops a distinct degenerate shortcut: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, or tautological collapse, all invisible to execution-based evaluation, which registers success regardless of whether the proof reflects genuine derivation.

\paragraph{The execution-only blind spot.}
Prove rate, the dominant evaluation metric for neurosymbolic formalizers~\citep{logic-lm, linc, satlm}, conflates faithful reasoning with degenerate shortcuts, a gap especially consequential under RL, where the optimizer exploits any shortcut the reward fails to penalize~\citep{skalse-reward-hacking, reward-hacking-survey}.
Recent work applies GRPO~\citep{deepseekmath} to train LLMs that generate solver-verified formal programs~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl} using binary execution feedback; this drives rapid PR gains but provides no signal on structural quality.
Process reward models~\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd} require expensive annotations and do not transfer to arbitrary solver-backed settings.
A separate line of work documents that LLMs already game logical formalization at inference time~\citep{kim-game-formalization, bondarenko-spec-gaming}; what is missing is an annotation-free \emph{diagnostic} for structural integrity in neurosymbolic outputs.

\paragraph{Component necessity testing.}
We address this gap with \emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), which applies \emph{component necessity testing} (leave-one-out ablation on solver inputs) to quantify structural integrity (Figure~\ref{fig:sta-overview}).
For each proved formalization, STA removes each component individually and re-runs the solver; the fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), with $\text{ISR}{=}1$ indicating full necessity and $\text{ISR}{=}0$ complete redundancy.
LOO ablation itself is standard~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; our contribution lies in applying it as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and in the empirical phenomena it surfaces.
ISR captures structural rather than semantic integrity (downstream NLI: $\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$).

\paragraph{ISR as diagnostic.}
As a post-hoc diagnostic on a GRPO formalizer trained with FOLIO~\citep{folio}, ISR reveals a structural collapse trajectory invisible to PR: $\text{ISR}^{*}{:}\,0.642\to 0.132\to 0.003$ over 100--1000 steps (seed~42; 99.5\% degradation) while PR rises $32\%{\to}96\%$.
Three seeds diverge radically (PR $\sigma{=}47$\,pp), each converging to a qualitatively different mode: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, and tautological collapse.
An SFT baseline on identical data reaches $\text{PR}{=}13.0\%$ with 92.3\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps), localizing the failure to RL optimization, not data or capacity.

\paragraph{ISR as reward: inevitable Goodhart collapse.}
Repurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\text{exec}} \cdot (1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, ISR contains an inherent structural vulnerability: tautological proofs (a single premise identical to the conclusion) receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction, and implication tautologies ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during GRPO rollouts~\citep{karwowski-goodhart-rl, kwa-catastrophic-goodhart}.
This makes Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} inevitable at every tested dose ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$): $\beta$ controls \emph{when} collapse occurs, not \emph{whether}.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, collapse is stochastic and delayed: 5 seeds bifurcate between rapid H7 convergence (2 seeds, ${\leq}100$ steps) and a transient genuine window (${\sim}23\%$ non-hacking at 500 steps, 5-seed pooled) that closes under extended training ($17\%{\to}2\%$ genuine at 1000 steps).
Snapshot evaluation at 500 steps would overestimate ISR's benefit; trajectory analysis reveals the window is temporary.
The effect transfers to Prolog (3/3 seeds yield 0\% non-hacking via distinct mechanisms, including \emph{query-as-fact gaming}) and across model scale (1.7B discovers qualitatively novel gaming modes).
ISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \emph{reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer at any dose.}

\paragraph{Contributions.}
Across 6 reward conditions, 5 seeds, 2 logic types, 2 model scales, and up to 1000 steps, we contribute: (\textbf{C1}) ISR as a diagnostic for GRPO reward hacking, with a 99.5\% collapse trajectory invisible to PR and an SFT control localizing the failure to RL (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}); (\textbf{C2}) an empirical instance of inevitable Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: ISR's structural bias toward tautology ($\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ for $P{\to}P$) creates a positive feedback loop that causes gaming at all four tested doses; collapse is stochastic and delayed at moderate $\beta$ but trajectory analysis confirms all seeds converge, showing that $\beta$ controls timing, not outcome (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); (\textbf{C3}) cross-logic transfer to Prolog with consistent Goodhart effects across all seeds (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}); (\textbf{C4}) a nine-mode hacking taxonomy including query-as-fact gaming, obfuscated tautology, and a scale-specific \emph{ex falso} mode, motivating functional cross-validation of diagnostics (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
These are cautionary results: snapshot evaluation of structural rewards can overestimate their benefit; only trajectory analysis reveals inevitable collapse.

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides, while SFT localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR exhibits inevitable Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR (${\geq}0.5$ by construction), creating a positive feedback loop that causes gaming at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$).
The effect is consistent across logic types (Prolog: 0\% non-hacking, 3/3 seeds), model scales (1.7B: novel gaming modes), and training durations (500$\to$1000 steps: transient genuine windows close).
ISR semantics are objective-dependent: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals redundancy; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals metric gaming.

\paragraph{Timing, not destiny.}
$\beta$ does not control whether collapse occurs, but when.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, 5 seeds bifurcate stochastically: 2 collapse rapidly (${\leq}150$ steps), 3 sustain a transient genuine window (5-seed pooled: ${\sim}23\%$; per non-collapsed seed: $17$--$55\%$) that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary ($17\%{\to}2\%$ at 1000 steps).
At $\beta{=}0.05$, the single tested seed collapses immediately (100\% H7); at $\beta{=}0.2$, all 3 seeds collapse; at $\beta{=}0.3$, diverse failure modes emerge.
The structural bias ($P{\to}P$ receives $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, single-premise-equals-conclusion receives $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$) ensures that H7 tautology is always the global ISR-maximizing exploit.
Once a seed samples and reinforces this exploit, convergence is irreversible; $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling.

\paragraph{Classifier blind spots.}
H7b (obfuscated tautology) and Prolog query-as-fact gaming demonstrate that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots exploitable by optimization.
In both cases, functional LOO analysis exposed gaming invisible to surface-level detection: H7b via vacuous quantifier wrapping ($10/12$ at $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$, triple gaming of execution, ISR, and classifier), query-as-fact via $95/97$ tautological samples the strict classifier labeled non-hacking (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
H9 (contradiction injection, 1.7B Random $\beta{=}0.1$; \S\ref{sec:crossscale}) extends this pattern further: contradictory premises register as individually necessary under LOO, bypassing both text-match and functional $n_{\text{necessary}}$ classifiers; detection requires logic-level consistency checking.
These cases collectively argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of text-based hacking classifiers, complemented by logic-level checks for novel exploit classes.

\paragraph{Capacity-dependent Goodhart basins.}
Different model capacities converge to different exploit strategies under identical reward formulations (\S\ref{sec:crossscale}): 4B frequently converges to H7 (tautological duplication) or H1 (conclusion embedding) depending on seed, while 1.7B discovers H9 (contradiction explosion, under random) or fixed-template H1 (under ISR, zero-variance $\text{ISR}{=}0.6$).
No safe scale exists; both model sizes achieve 0\% non-hacking at $\beta{=}0.1$.
This suggests that scaling model capacity does not eliminate Goodhart effects but shifts the exploit basin.

\paragraph{Snapshot evaluation is misleading.}
At 500 steps, ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ shows ${\sim}23\%$ genuine output (5-seed pooled), while 2/5 seeds have already collapsed to 0\%.
A practitioner evaluating at this checkpoint would conclude ISR provides moderate structural benefit; the 1000-step trajectory reveals this is a temporal artifact.
This has practical implications: any evaluation of structural rewards must include trajectory analysis or extended training to distinguish transient from stable improvement.
The ISR/PR ratio (stable at ${\sim}0.30$ during SFT, collapsing during RL gaming) may serve as an early-stopping signal for Goodhart onset.

\paragraph{Hacking mode switching is seed-dependent.}
The dominant hacking mode (H7 vs.\ H1) is determined by random initialization, not reward condition: under identical configurations, different seeds converge to qualitatively different modes (Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}).
Random $\beta{=}0.1$ across 4 seeds yields genuine rates from $1\%$ to $23\%$ ($8.2{\pm}9.7$\,pp, $\text{CV}{>}1$); ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ shows even greater variance (0\% to ${\sim}55\%$ genuine at 500 steps, 5 seeds).
Single-seed results can misrepresent a reward configuration's hacking profile; multi-seed evaluation with trajectory analysis should be standard.

\paragraph{Future directions.}
The asymmetry (reliable observer, unreliable optimizer at any dose) may generalize to other perturbation-based diagnostics; ISR and similar metrics should serve as post-hoc evaluation tools, not training signals.
The stochastic bifurcation mechanism suggests that gated ISR (activating structural reward only after a warmstart period, or deactivating once ISR exceeds a threshold) might extend the genuine window, though the inherent structural bias makes indefinite stability unlikely.
Future work should target gaming-robust reward designs that do not reward tautological constructions, broader logic types, and formal analysis of the bifurcation dynamics.
